system.name: A3 (Any-order Any-subset Autoregressive modeling)
system.one_liner: A generalised autoregressive framework with two-stream attention that predicts arbitrary token groups in any order, adapted progressively from pretrained AR models.

content.variant_note: bottom-up forward pass of one toy sentence: tokens, embedding, an xL two-stream attention block drawn as two mask grids, then the CE loss
content.argues: Group-wise causal masks in two-stream attention let an AR model predict token groups in any order: content stream sees own and earlier groups, query stream only earlier ones.
content.subject: Forward pass of A3's two-stream attention on a six-token sentence split into three groups, drawn as mask grids.

encoding.color_means: Teal = group G1, purple = group G3, orange = group G2, kept on tokens, hidden states, brackets, axis numbers and thick mask outlines. Blue mask cell = 0 (may attend), white = -inf (blocked). Grey-blue = query-stream states.
encoding.line_style_means: Dashed vertical line separates the two streams; thick coloured outlines mark the diagonal own-group blocks; hollow block arrows carry tensors between stages.
encoding.shape_means: Adjacent cells in a row = sequence of tokens or states; 6x6 grid = attention mask (Q rows by K columns); rounded frame with x L = repeated layers.
encoding.marker_means: G1-G3 name the token groups; 1-6 index positions; Q and K label mask axes and arrows (Q, K, V) say what each stream receives.
encoding.emphasis: The two mask grids are the largest items and differ only in the own-group blocks, which carry thick coloured outlines, so the rule 'own group visible or not' is the first thing seen.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give every token group one colour and keep it on the tokens, the states, the group braces and the outline of its block in the mask grids, so a pair of small grids explains a masking rule without a key. Draw the two variants as equal grids side by side so only the changed cells differ.
lessons.suits: Attention-mask or block-sparse architectures where a toy sequence and its grouping explain which positions may see which.

sections: Two-stream Attention Design for Any-order Prediction (p.4)
evidence: The model employs a two-stream attention module with distinct causal masks.
Blue entries in the attention mask denote 0, and white entries denote −∞.

summary: A3 (Any-order Any-subset Autoregressive modeling) generalises autoregressive language modeling to arbitrary token groups and generation orders, adapting pretrained AR models with a two-stream attention design borrowed from XLNet. Figure 1 draws one forward pass on the toy sentence 'The answer is 14 inches long', split into groups G1, G3 and G2 that keep one colour everywhere. Tokens pass through an Embedding box into hidden states and then into an 'x L' frame holding two 6x6 mask grids: the content stream (Q, K, V) sees its own and all earlier groups, the query stream (Q, with K, V from the content stream) only earlier groups. The query output is compared with the target tokens by a CE loss. Flat vector, draw.io look, hand-drawn font, hollow block arrows.
summary_zh: A3 模型的前向过程图：示例句子被分成 G1、G3、G2 三组，经 Embedding 后进入 ×L 的双流注意力块，用两张 6×6 掩码网格分别表示内容流与查询流，输出与目标词做交叉熵损失，组别用颜色贯穿全图。
notes: The pre-screen counted 2 panels; the two streams share one rounded frame and a dashed divider and have no separate frames, so panel_count is 1 and they are recorded as lanes. worked-walkthrough is secondary: one toy sentence runs through the whole pass, but it is drawn once, not redrawn per step. The subscript of the H(i) glyphs (math drawn as paths) could not be read reliably, so element names use H(i).
